headline: No shared channels or writable surfaces are documented; the pair is low-risk overall, with only speculative prompt/cascade paths from content-writing to email-scheduling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser that would let awesome-prompts inject instructions into awesome-python. Both show network_egress:none and empty io_surfaces, so a direct prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared clipboard and shared workspace access.
Do not pipe raw outputs from awesome-prompts into awesome-python prompts.
Add provenance labels if a bridge is later introduced.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at any future integration point.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no data classes touched, no shared workspace, and no network egress for either awesome-prompts or awesome-python. With no documented sensitive data flow, leakage between them is not plausible from the provided evidence.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any future shared directory.
Keep both agents on separate accounts or containers.
Review any added upload or sync feature before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add access controls if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts and awesome-python are both documented as non-runnable open-source listings with empty concurrency_model and no write or network permissions. No overlapping mutable resource or lockless write path is documented, so capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either profile gains filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scopes, conflict analysis should be repeated.
mitigations: Do not treat these listings as concurrently writable agents.
Keep any future mutable resources separate per agent.
Document ownership before enabling shared writes.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented execution path where awesome-prompts produces operational output that awesome-python consumes as authoritative input. Both profiles are non-runnable listings with no io_surfaces, so a cascade from one into the other is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF a workflow is created where outputs from awesome-prompts are automatically fed into awesome-python actions, cascade risk becomes relevant.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing any generated content.
Do not auto-execute downstream actions from prompt collections.
Label any future handoff as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking integrations.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling differences are documented for either awesome-prompts or awesome-python. With empty data_classes_touched and docs-only evidence, there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the pair alone.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or financial records, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Record any future retention or residency settings before deployment.
Verify legal basis before enabling data collection.
requires-engineering: implement policy controls if regulated data is introduced.
